summary: Gé Mang Khenchen Yönten Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab.

Specializing in Indology, Gérard Colas held posts as Directeur de recherche and Senior Fellow at the CNRS (attested 2004, 2009), as well as Directeur de recherche CNRS at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences (attested 2012).

Specializing in Indology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Gérard Fussman studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1961–1965). He served as head at the CNRS (~1984–1999) and became Professeur at the Collège de France in 1984.
Working in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics, Gérard Huet studied under George Ernst (~1970–1972) and Maurice Nivat (~1972–1976). He served as a professor at Inria from around 1974.

Specializing in Tibetology and Indology, Géza Bethlenfalvy studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1956–1963) under Lajos Ligeti. His career included posts at the University of Delhi (1970), Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna (2007–2008).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Gösta Liebert studied at Lund University and the University of Gothenburg under Hjalmar Frisk, Nils Holmer, and Stig Wikander. He held posts at Lund, Uppsala, and notably Gothenburg as professor (1955–1982).

Working in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Götz von Selle studied at Berlin, Kiel, and Göttingen (Dr. phil.). He held library and professorial posts at Göttingen and served as professor and library deputy director at Königsberg (~1938–1945).
Günter Blamberger held a post at the University of Kassel (~1994–1995) and became Chair in German Philology at the University of Cologne around 1995.
Active in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Günter Grönbold worked at the Bavarian State Library from around 1975 to 2008, serving as head of its Oriental Section (~1978–2008).

Active in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Günter Schweiger studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business under doctoral supervisor Gert Klingenschmitt. He served as full professor at the Vienna University of Economics and Business (1974–2009).

Linguist H. Craig Melchert studied at Michigan State University, the Defense Language Institute, the National Cryptologic School, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1978–2007) and UCLA (2007–2015).

Indologist H. G. Narahari studied at the University of Mysore and the University of Madras, where C. Kunhan Raja supervised his MA (1939). In 1944, he was attested as a Research Fellow at Madras and Research Assistant at Adyar Library.
Specializing in history and archaeology, H. J. de Graaf studied at Leiden University (~1919–1926) and under Poerbatjaraka (1927–1930).
Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, H. Kikuchi was attested in 1966 as a research student at the University of Delhi, where he studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale.
Specializing in Indology and linguistics, H. Sesha Aiyangar held posts in the Kannada (Canarese) Department at the University of Madras, attested in 1938 and 1957.
Working in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, H. V. Nagaraja Rao held positions at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore and as a professor at the University of Mysore (attested 2012).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Hae-ju Sunim was a visiting lecturer at Harvard University (1996–1997) and Associate Professor of Buddhist Studies at Dongguk University (attested 1999).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Haiyan Hu-von Hinüber completed her MA at Peking University (-1982) under Kemo Jin and also studied under Zhongxin Jiang. In 2010, she was Director at the University of Freiburg.

Specializing in linguistics and Tibetology, Hajime Kitamura studied at Tokyo under Tokan Tada. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1964–1986), Reitaku University (1986), and served as president of Toyo Bunko (1990–2001).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Hajime Nakamura studied at the University of Tokyo under Hakuju Ui. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1954–1973) and founded and directed the Eastern Institute (Toho Gakuin).
